title: San Diego's core public data on first launch
summary: While your library has no imported tables, the overview offers to fetch the City of San Diego's budget, actuals, Get It Done and SDPD calls tables so the leads under What stands out have something to read. It is offered once, and a download that leaves any table unimported is reported until you close it.

sections.heading: What it fetches
paragraphs: The City's operating budget and operating actuals for every published fiscal year, the Get It Done reports open today for every service, the Encampment reports closed in each year from 2022 to this year so far, and SDPD calls for service for last year and this year so far. Each table is fetched and imported the same way as Fetch and import in Analysis, one at a time.

Each line names the leads it feeds. The budget feeds Adopted and actual spending, Budget, Encampment reports and shelter beds by year, and the department beside a service-report lead; the actuals feed Adopted and actual spending and the settlement accounts; the open and closed Get It Done reports feed the service-report leads and the Encampment reports in the budget and beds comparison. The calls for service feed the calls lead: how SLEEPER, check-the-welfare, trespassing, 5150 and 647F calls ended, and the beats SLEEPER calls came from.

The closed years start at 2022 because the comparison counts the reports filed in a fiscal year only when every closed-year file from the year it began is imported, and the shelter inventory's last count is January 2024. Fiscal 2023 and 2024 are the two years it can compare, which takes every closed file from 2022 on.

Each table shows its own outcome: waiting, fetching, the number of rows imported, or the reason it was not imported. A table that fails does not stop the others. This year's files hold the year so far, and a file the City has not yet published for the new year is reported as not imported.

sections.heading: Where the data comes from
paragraphs: Every table is retrieved at that moment from the City of San Diego open data portal (data.sandiego.gov). The City publishes these datasets in the public domain under the Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (ODC-PDDL 1.0), for information only and without warranty.

Shelter beds are not fetched here. The emergency shelter inventory is published by UCSD's Homelessness Hub, from the Regional Task Force on Homelessness count, with no licence stated. Until you fetch it, Budget, Encampment reports and shelter beds by year shows under What stands out as missing data, the emergency shelter inventory, with a button to fetch it; once it is imported the comparison runs on the tables already fetched.

sections.heading: When it is offered
paragraphs: Only when the library has finished loading and holds no imported tables. Choosing Skip, or a download that finishes, settles the offer; starting the download does not. You can fetch any of these tables later from Analysis.

The download continues if you leave the overview. When every table is imported the app opens Analysis, unless you have moved to another view meanwhile. If any table failed, or the app closed before the download reached it, the card says the library is incomplete, lists those tables and offers to get the missing ones until you close it. Each failure is also written to the activity log.
